title: install.sh: can_prompt must fail-safe when /dev/tty exists but cannot open
action: Bug (live repro in this sandbox): can_prompt() tests [ -r /dev/tty ] && [ -w /dev/tty ] which PASS in sandboxed shells where /dev/tty exists but open() fails => confirm() writes to /dev/tty (error), read fails, then 'answer: unbound variable' crash under set -u — instead of the designed fail-safe 'no TTY to ask. Re-run with --yes'. Fix: (1) can_prompt() must attempt a real open: [ -r /dev/tty ] && [ -w /dev/tty ] && ( : </dev/tty ) 2>/dev/null; (2) harden the read: IFS= read -r answer < /dev/tty || answer='' so a mid-read failure can never hit set -u. Mode-gate record: tiny — 1 product file, 0 risk flags, one direct task; red-first evidence = the live crash observed 2026-07-26 (line 101-103 '/dev/tty: No such device or address' + 'answer: unbound variable'). Verify = repro turns into the designed failure message. REGEN OBLIGATION (after the fix): node scripts/render_plugin_skill_trees.mjs, then node packages/bee/scripts/onboard_bee.mjs --repo-root . --apply, then node scripts/release_manifest.mjs --write.

truths: non-tty run WITHOUT --yes exits 1 with the designed 'Re-run with --yes' message, zero 'unbound variable'
prohibitions: no behavior change beyond the prompt guard
no edits to install.ps1 (its Confirm-Step has no such bug)
